The agent platform gave developers a dedicated home for the fastest-growing workload type in AI, with one-click deployments on decentralized compute out of the box. The marketplace mechanism works through a reverse auction: tenants submit deployment requests specifying their compute requirements (CPU cores, RAM, storage, GPU type), and providers bid on those requests. The tenant selects the best bid — typically the lowest price that meets their requirements — and the deployment begins. This competitive bidding is what drives Akash prices significantly below centralized cloud providers.

As of May 21, 2026 (UTC), CoinMarketCap data shows AKT at $0.7695 with a $226.22M market cap. The 5.83% vol/mkt cap ratio ($13.19M volume on $226.22M market cap) is moderate — indicating steady trading activity without the extreme volatility of newer tokens.

### The Cosmos SDK foundation [...] ### What is Akash Network (AKT) and what does it do?

Akash Network is a decentralized cloud computing marketplace on the Cosmos blockchain. It connects tenants (users who need compute) with providers (data centers and individuals with spare capacity) through a reverse auction mechanism. Tenants deploy containerized applications using SDL files, providers bid on deployments, and the network settles payments in AKT or other IBC tokens. Key use cases include AI model training and inference, web hosting, and any containerized application. As of May 21, 2026 (UTC), AKT trades at $0.7695, market cap $226.22M, rank #136, with 293.97M of 388.53M tokens in circulation (75.66%).

### How does Akash Network compare to AWS and Google Cloud? [...] Akash Network (AKT) is a decentralized cloud computing marketplace built on the Cosmos SDK — it connects users who need compute resources (tenants) with providers who have idle server capacity (providers), creating a permissionless spot market for CPU, GPU, and storage. The core value proposition is cost: Akash claims 85% lower prices than AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure by monetizing underutilized data center capacity that would otherwise sit idle. In 2025-2026, Akash has become one of the primary DePIN (Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Network) plays for AI compute — GPU availability on Akash has become a meaningful alternative to centralized cloud providers for AI model training and inference workloads. ### Confidential Compute via Kata Containers

Completion Date: 7/17/2026

This AEP defines how tenants request confidential computing workloads on Akash Network and how providers advertise confidential compute capabilities. Tenants set `params.tee` in their SDL to either `cpu` or `cpu-gpu` to request confidential compute. The provider determines the actual TEE platform (AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX) at deployment time based on its hardware. Workloads run inside Kata Containers (micro-VMs) on TEE-capable providers.
